clue.text: Abreast of method for FA Cup draw?

blocks.note: first meaning: next to each other, level
second meaning, read literally: teams (sides) are drawn out one after another, one side then the next

explanation.walkthrough: The FA Cup is English football's knockout competition, whose fixtures are drawn by pulling teams' balls out of a bag; a team is a 'side'. The question mark flags the playful literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the ordinary idiom for being positioned alongside one another, which is exactly what abreast means.

clue.text: Complaint letters periodically dispatched from island

indicators.note: sending letters away at regular intervals throws out every other one and keeps the rest

blocks.note: every other letter is sent away, starting with the first, leaving the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Someone's grumbling letters are sent off the island at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: SAD is seasonal affective disorder, the winter depression, so a 'complaint' in the sense of an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint here means an illness or disorder, and seasonal affective disorder is a recognised medical condition.

clue.text: Drop key objective following board's conclusion

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
following means coming after, so the key and objective are placed second, behind the board's last letter

blocks.note: the final letter of board
the Escape key on a computer keyboard
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A company abandons its key aim after the board reaches a decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' places the key and the objective after the board's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop and to descend are both verbs for going down to a lower level.

clue.text: Smashed gun having incurred fine

indicators.note: to incur something is to take it on, so the gun takes another word inside itself

blocks.note: the Bren gun, a British light machine gun
fine in the sense of all right

explanation.surface: A firearm smashed up, with its owner landed with a fine as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something smashed has been shattered into pieces, which is the basic sense of broken.

clue.text: TV programme broadcast about hospital

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, i.e. sow
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A television series is aired that is set in a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like it belongs to the TV picture, but it is the farming sense, scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A show is any programme on television, from a quiz to a drama.

clue.text: Blue bottle getting passed around

indicators.note: around means one word encircles the other, holding it inside

blocks.note: passed as in passed away
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage, i.e. spirit

explanation.surface: A blue glass bottle is handed round a group.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, 'bottle' means courage, as in 'he lost his bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in the sense of low-spirited or downhearted, the same mood as dispirited.

clue.text: Create an impression in France and Switzerland

blocks.note: et is French for and
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: Making a mark on people in two European countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is read as 'and' in France, followed by Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut lines into a surface with acid or a tool, literally creating an impression.

clue.text: Article about list circulating in plant

indicators.note: circulating suggests moving round and round, so the letters get mixed up
about means around, so the article wraps round the other letters

blocks.note: the definite article
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a list being passed round inside a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' tempts as a factory in the surface; it is the botanical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The thistle is a prickly flowering plant, the national emblem of Scotland.

clue.text: Manual workers describing case for historians?

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

blocks.note: the front of the case
describing the case in words gives 'H and S', so the joining word itself is used
the back of the case

explanation.surface: Labourers who write up a legal case for academic historians.
explanation.walkthrough: The outside letters of 'historians' are H and S; describing them in words gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands is the long-standing term for labourers or crew, as in farmhands or all hands on deck.

clue.text: Club's record number of points at start of season

blocks.note: a gramophone record is a disc

blocks.clueFragment: number of points at start of season
blocks.note: every team starts the season on nil points, and nil is the round letter O

explanation.surface: A football club's tally of points at the beginning of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a sports team, but it is a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a club or venue where people dance to recorded pop music.

clue.text: Regularly lobby meeting with passion

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
a session is a sitting or meeting

explanation.surface: Campaigners routinely lobby a committee meeting with real fervour.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is a consuming passion, an interest that dominates the mind.

clue.text: Master trained pupils of similar ability

indicators.note: trained suggests being drilled into a new shape, so the letters are reformed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster has trained up a set of similarly able pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' looks like the teacher in the scene, but it is just the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools a stream is a class grouping children of similar ability.

clue.text: Waited in line by indicated entrance for audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so we want what the word sounds like rather than its spelling

blocks.note: an actor is cued when signalled to come on stage

explanation.surface: Theatregoers lined up beside a signposted doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' and 'audience' paint a theatre queue, but it is the actor's entrance being signalled.
explanation.definitionFit: To queue is to wait in a line, so waited in line is the past tense.

clue.text: University dons question answer following drink

blocks.note: Q is the abbreviation for question
U is the abbreviation for university
A is the abbreviation for answer
ff. is the abbreviation for 'and the following pages'

explanation.surface: Academics question an answer given after a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: University dons are lecturers in the surface; here 'dons' means puts on, so U is attached to Q.
explanation.definitionFit: To quaff is to drink heartily, so it can stand in for the verb drink.

clue.text: Plane's speed cuts journeys to new destination

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it

blocks.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane; the 's adds S
a rate is a speed

explanation.surface: An aircraft's speed shortens trips to a fresh destination.
explanation.definitionFit: To migrate is to move to a new place to live, especially seasonally, as birds do.

clue.text: Demoralised person in divorce case losing right to support daughter

indicators.note: losing something means it drops out of the word

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
the respondent is the party a divorce petition is brought against
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A dejected party in a divorce loses the right to pay maintenance for their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it, so D goes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Despondent means having lost hope or heart, which is what being demoralised is.

clue.text: Unveiled female personal assistant

indicators.note: removing a veil uncovers what is underneath, so the outer letters come off

blocks.note: a maiden is a young woman

explanation.surface: A woman's personal assistant appears without her veil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unveiled' suggests a bride, which points the way to a maiden.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is an assistant to an important person, such as a minister's aide.

clue.text: Dodgy case edited names author recognised?

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters are put into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shaky legal case edited the names of those an author acknowledged.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase: the people named in a book's dedication.
explanation.definitionFit: Dedicatees are the people a book is dedicated to, so they are names an author has honoured.

clue.text: Put on period drama here?

blocks.note: first meaning: to mount a theatrical production
second meaning: a phase or step in a process
a third hint: a play is performed on this platform

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as staging a costume drama; 'period' is detached from 'drama' to stand alone, and 'drama here?' is an extra cryptic nod.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for producing a play and as a noun for a phase of development.

clue.text: Pet butterfly?

blocks.note: first meaning: to caress an animal
second meaning: a swimming style

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a butterfly kept as a pet; the question mark hints at the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroke an animal is to pet it, and the butterfly is one of the four competitive swimming strokes.

clue.text: Writer left out correcting fluid having erased last name

indicators.note: out as in out of order, so the letters are rearranged
erasing the last letter and writing something in its place swaps one letter for another

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
Tipp-Ex is a brand of correction fluid
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An author leaves out the correction fluid after erasing a surname.
explanation.walkthrough: N replaces the final X of Tipp-Ex, a correction-fluid brand well known in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tip pen is a writing implement, and a writer can mean the thing you write with.

clue.text: The new girl ordered sandwiches containing less fat

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters before it are recast
ordered means put into a different arrangement
a sandwich holds its filling between two outer parts

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A new girl at work orders sandwiches with a lower-fat filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighter food has fewer calories, and 'light' on a label means reduced fat.

clue.text: Members of Black Sabbath joined famous group

indicators.note: members are parts of a whole, so a run of letters inside the next word is taken

blocks.note: the letters sit inside the band's second word, from its second to fifth letter

explanation.surface: Musicians from the heavy-metal band Black Sabbath joined another celebrated band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black' is surface dressing; the letters sit inside the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Abba are the Swedish pop quartet who won Eurovision in 1974, a world-famous band.

clue.text: Relevance of reporter's exposé …

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the news, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: an exposé lays something bare

explanation.surface: How a journalist's revelation matters, continued into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the sentence on into 23 Down, but the two clues are solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing means connection or relevance, as in 'this has no bearing on the case'.

clue.text: … leads to some papers linking burnt remains in prominent story

indicators.note: leads are the front-runners, so the first letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: first letters of the three words
ash is what is left after burning

explanation.surface: The reporter's exposé makes the lead in several papers, tying charred evidence into a front-page story.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is journalists' slang for the main front-page story, given the biggest headline.

clue.text: Foreign Office certain about government leader being detained by undesirable elements

indicators.note: about means around, so the combined letters surround another piece
'leader' keeps only the first letter of 'government'

blocks.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office
bound as in certain or sure to happen
the leading letter of government

explanation.surface: A diplomat is sure the head of state is being held by unsavoury types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undesirable elements' sounds like criminals; it is weather, the elements. The Foreign Office is Britain's ministry for overseas affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fogbound means unable to travel because of fog, so held up by bad weather.

clue.text: Group assembled for collective action in favour of church

blocks.note: for meaning supporting
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A congregation gathers to campaign in support of their church.
explanation.definitionFit: A force is a body of people organised to act together, such as a police force or task force.

clue.text: Promote potential partner's report on latest developments

blocks.note: to promote someone is to move them up
someone you go on a date with

explanation.surface: Talking up a prospective partner's account of recent news.
explanation.definitionFit: An update is a bulletin bringing someone up to date on what has happened.

clue.text: Short month in which temperature rises a degree

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means moving higher up the column, so the letter is reinserted nearer the top

blocks.note: the short form of September
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A brief month in which the thermometer goes up one degree.
explanation.walkthrough: The T at the bottom of the month moves up two places.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is one grade or level on a scale, so it can mean a degree, as in 'by degrees'.

clue.text: Setter not being edited is extremely bad

indicators.note: editing changes and rearranges text, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler grumbles that refusing to be edited is a terrible idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Rottenest is the superlative of rotten, meaning very bad, so it is the worst of all.

clue.text: Peripheral characters killed in outstanding film

indicators.note: killing off the characters on the edge removes the outermost letters

blocks.note: salient means prominent or standing out

explanation.surface: Minor characters are killed off in a great movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people in the film; it means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien is Ridley Scott's 1979 science-fiction horror movie, so it fits the bare definition.

clue.text: Be critical of backing tipster's favourite

indicators.note: going backwards means the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: critics pan a show they dislike

explanation.surface: Criticise a racing tipster for supporting their top pick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like betting on a horse in the racing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A nap is a racing tipster's most confident selection of the day.

clue.text: Gain by Labour unseating new Liberal peer

indicators.note: unseating someone turns them out of their place so another can take it

blocks.note: to earn is to gain by working
N is the abbreviation for new
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Labour gains a seat by defeating a newly elected Liberal member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' and 'Liberal' read as British political parties; Labour is just work here.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman, and nobles who sit in the Lords are peers.

clue.text: Servant emptied heaviest containers brought round to supply what's lacking

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only the outside letters
turning the whole thing round means reading everything backwards

blocks.note: a page is a boy servant
only the first and last letters
pots hold things

explanation.surface: A servant empties the heaviest crates and brings them round to make up a shortfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emptied' applies to the word after it, while 'brought round' reverses the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop the gap means to fill a hole temporarily, a stopgap, providing what is missing.
